messages:
maria: Heads-up — onboarding a community MPT variant and seeing a weird eval regression after our hf->redwood convert run. :eyes:

maria: Symptoms: samples contain repeated "<|special_unk|>" tokens in the middle of sentences, and rouge/qa scores dropped ~8% after quant+convert. happened on both int8 and gptq experiments.

li: did you try running the tokenizer directly on the checkpoint? sometimes special tokens map gets lost on conversions.

maria: Yup, ran tokenizer.encode on some failing prompts. Found tokens that should be single ids are being emitted as two ids: looks like an offset of +1 for several special tokens.

alex: possible causes: 1) safetensors shard index reorder during download 2) weightname mapping script renamed keys inconsistently with revision pin fallback 3) special_tokens_map.json not included in the model card by the hub.

maria: Logs from converter: ````
INFO convert: loading shards: shards=4
WARN convert: shard 2 missing checksum, retrying
INFO convert: applying weightname-map v2 -> v2_renamed
INFO convert: writing tokenizer files
ERROR convert: special_tokens_map.json not found, falling back to defaults
````

li: Hmm, the fallback bit is suspicious. If special tokens default to reserved placeholders, the tokenizer vocab might shift if we also inserted/removed entries during weight remapping.

convert-bot: Note: revision pinning disabled for this run (policy=allow_latest). If hub-hosted shards changed order between revisions, checksum mismatch can cause reassembly with wrong index.

maria: I traced the safetensors index.json we cached vs direct-hub-head: ordering differs for two shards, and the converter's reassembly assumes stable index ordering. When reassembled with mismatched index, some token embeddings ended up in different rows -> downstream quantized model produced wrong token ids for specials.

alex: Oof. So it's not just tokenizer metadata missing, but physical embedding rows getting permuted. That would explain the token-id shift.

li: Repro steps?

maria: Steps I used: 1) hf_hub_download model repo (no revision pin) 2) run redwood-hf-convert --quantize gptq --output /tmp/mpt-conv 3) load with redwood runtime and run eval set.

maria: Quick fix I validated locally: pin revision explicitly to the commit hash, re-download all shards, then run converter with --validate-shard-checksums and --force-tokenizer-files. After that the special tokens are correct and evals return to baseline.

alex: Good find. Longer-term fixes: a) make converter refuse to proceed if shard index ordering differs from index.json checksums b) ensure weightname mapping is applied before any in-place reindexing c) write special_tokens_map.json into output even when missing, derived from vocab/specials detection.

li: Also add an integration test in the converter CI that simulates shard-order permute and ensures assembly is deterministic.

maria: I'm going to open a PR with: 1) stricter shard validation + clearer error msg, 2) fallback special token write, 3) docs note about always pinning hub revisions for conversion/quantization experiments.

maria: @alex can you eyeball the PR when I open? want to include weightname-map unit tests.

alex: Yeah will review. Also add a small eval hook that checks for unexpected token ids for known specials after conversion (fast sanity). :+1:

deploy-bot: Deployment note: converters deployed on staging; will run nightly with pinned revisions for existing repros.

maria: Thanks — filing issue and PR now. I'll paste links in thread. :face_with_monocle:
